result:
Everything is green across the whole workspace. Summary of the change:

**`Status` now sorts `cited` before `derived`** in `crates/smysl-core/src/types/epistemics.rs`, satisfying rule M's comparison order.

Key design decision: the wire discriminants (`as_u8`/`from_u8`) are normative per the format spec (§2.3) and shared across Rust, Python, Node, and Go implementations plus the published 1.3.0 conformance fixtures — so I left those untouched (`Derived = 3`, `Cited = 4` on the wire) rather than renumbering the raw discriminants, which would have silently broken every uid hash and cross-language fixture in the repo. Instead I decoupled `Ord`/`PartialOrd` from the wire discriminant via a new `Status::rank()` method and hand-written `Ord` impl, so comparisons (rule M, `Status::ALL` iteration order, etc.) now correctly place `Cited` below `Derived` while `as_u8()` stays pinned.

This does change real rule M/T semantics (a `derived` claim can no longer rest solely on a `cited` ground — `cited` is now the weaker one), which rippled into a handful of tests in `smysl-check` and `smysl-ingest` that encoded the old ordering; I updated those, plus regenerated the one committed, mechanically-generated schema fixture (`fixtures/schema/unit.json`) that embeds `Status::ALL`'s order.

Both required suites pass (`cargo test -q -p smysl --tests --no-fail-fast`, `cargo test -q -p smysl-core --no-fail-fast`), and I also verified the entire workspace (`cargo test --workspace --all-features`) is green and `cargo fmt`/`clippy` are clean. Nothing was committed, per your instructions.
